sections.heading: Summary
paragraphs: Per the file, serialize pointers for instruction accts to allow direct acct access without requiring parsing of the acct section. Those statements are the file’s claims, not a Sol.College measurement of a live cluster.

sections.heading: Motivation
paragraphs: Per the file, currently, sBPF programs in (per the file) ABIv1 must parse the accts section of the serialized (per the file) input region to extract acct boundary information so as to provide the program (per the file) with a slice of accts. Per the file, this parsing represents most (per the file) of the entrypoint's cost. Per the file, since acct boundaries are already known (per the file) to the VM when (per the file) preparing the program input, (per the file) they can instead be (per the file) serialized directly into the input. Per the file, this lets the entrypoint to derive the accts slice without iterating over or parsing the accts section. Per the file, as a result, the (per the file) entrypoint consumes a constant (per the file) number of compute units, (per the file) independent of the number of accts. Those statements are the file’s claims, not a Sol.College measurement of a live cluster.

sections.heading: New Terminology
paragraphs: Per the file, **accts slice pointer**: A slice (per the file) of 64-bit (8-byte) pointers, (per the file) with one pointer per instruction acct, stored at the end of the (per the file) program input parameters. Those statements are the file’s claims, not a Sol.College measurement of a live cluster.

sections.heading: Detailed Design
paragraphs: Per the file, when the feature is (per the file) activated, the VM serializes the slice of acct pointers after the program (per the file) ID in the program (per the file) input parameters for any (per the file) ABIv1 program (i.e., those that fail to use Loader v1). Per the file, all other parameters remain unchanged: Each acct pointer is the address (per the file) (u64 little-endian) of the (per the file) first byte of the acct information. Per the file, they all has to be valid addresses within the input section. Per the file, duplicated accts will have the same (per the file) pointer value, i.e., they (per the file) will point to the same acct. Per the file, these are the same (per the file) addresses that entrypoints previously (per the file) had to compute when parsing the accts section, but it is (per the file) now provided directly as an input parameter.

Per the file, the slice of acct pointers is made available (per the file) to all ABIv1 programs, (per the file) under all loaders, regardless (per the file) of whether it is read or not. Per the file, since this data is (per the file) appended after the standard (per the file) input parameters, existing programs are unaffected. Per the file, given that, after SIMD-0321 is activated, programs will receive (per the file) a direct pointer to the (per the file) instruction data, programs can derive (per the file) the location of the slice of acct pointers without parsing the accts section: read the number of accts from r1. read the length (per the file) of the instruction data from (per the file) r2 - 8. pass the following (per the file) three references to the program entrypoint: program_id: a &[u8] slice created (per the file) from r2 + <length of the instruction (per the file) data> with length equal to 32 bytes. accts: a &[AccountView] slice created from r2 (per the file) + <length of the instruction data> + 32 (per the file) + padding with length equal to <number of accts>. instruction_data: a &[u8] slice created from (per the file) r2 with length equal to <length of (per the file) instruction data>.

sections.heading: Backwards Compatibility
